title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Ramesh
description:
Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost while preserving latency SLOs by shipping sensible defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, adding model-specific quantization profiles, and wiring unit-economic (UEcon) tooling into the autotune flow. This PR is the follow-up to ENG-1428 and ties together: 1) defaults that make autotune a safe opt-in for new model routes, 2) per-model quantization profile support and validation, and 3) a lightweight UEcon CLI and export for reporting/analysis.

What this changes: - runtime: adds a DefaultServingConfig that encodes conservative batching window, max_batch_size, and prefix cache TTL tuned from recent perf canary results; routes without explicit config will inherit these defaults. - batching scheduler: change to allow soft-latency targets (target_percentile and slack) so autotune can trade cost vs tail latency smoother. - kv cache manager: introduce prefix-based TTL heuristics and a cache-size hint exported to planners. - quant profiles: new YAML profiles per model family (gpt-2/3-like, transformer-xl variants, llama-family) plus validation and fallback to float16 when profile fails. - uecon tooling: new CLI under tools/uecon that queries recent CPU/GPU token counts, request shapes, and computes per-route unit cost estimates. It emits a JSON report that the autotune service consumes to recommend quant/batch/cache combos. - docs: cost-optimization.md with rollout guidance and example Linear links for evaluation sets.

Testing & rollout plan: unit + integration + perf canary on staging. Default-serving-config is gated behind feature flag (autotune_defaults_enabled) for 2 weeks staged rollout (canary -> 50% -> 100%). Quant profiles are additive and applied only when tenant permits quantization. UEcon export available to internal dashboards; we will run a 7-day analysis to validate predicted vs actual unit-cost changes.

Checklist:
- [x] Add defaults and feature flag
- [x] Implement quant profile schema + validation
- [x] UEcon CLI and exporter
- [x] Unit & integration tests
- [x] Perf canary configs and results attached
- [x] Docs and release notes

Related: ENG-1428, ENG-1482, PM-3404.

release_notes: Ship conservative autotune defaults for batching and prefix caching; add model quantization profiles with validation and safe fallbacks; include unit-economics (UEcon) exporter to inform autotune recommendations. Expect ~6-12% token cost reduction in workloads that leverage quantization + tuned batching; rollout behind feature flag.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: autotune_defaults_enabled (false -> true rollout). Watch metrics: per-route token cost, 95th tail latency, error-rate spike. Rollback: disable feature flag and revert route-server config if increased errors observed.
perf_summary: Staging perf canary (72h): median latency +2ms, p95 +7ms, token-cost -8.3% aggregated across write-heavy routes. Quantized routes showed -15% compute cost but required careful validation. See attached perf artifacts in PR for full breakdown.
